title: Optimizing Team Behavior via Extremum-seeking Control in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
title_zh: 通过极值寻优控制在多智能体强化学习中优化团队行为

paragraphs.en: In cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), agents must learn to coordinate their actions to achieve shared objectives. A key indicator of effective coordination is behavioral diversity, i.e., the agents’ potential to enact distinct yet complementary control policies given the same set of observations. Although behavioral diversity can enable role specialization and richer joint behaviors, its appropriate level is highly context- and task-dependent and often costly to tune. We propose Adaptive Diversity Control (ADiCo), a two-timescale framework that adapts behavioral diversity online during training. On a fast timescale, Diversity Control (DiCo) regulates system diversity toward a target value. On a slower timescale, an Extremum Seeking Controller (ESC) adjusts this target using only mean episodic returns, without requiring an explicit model or analytical gradient of the diversity-performance landscape. We evaluate ADiCo on six configurations across two cooperative MARL tasks, where it maintains task-appropriate diversity levels: low diversity when homogeneous policies are beneficial and higher diversity when heterogeneous policies are required. Through this adaptation, ADiCo matches or exceeds the mean performance of DiCo (best grid-searched diversity target) and Unconstrained DiCo (diversity allowed to emerge without target regulation). These results demonstrate that incorporating classical feedback control into MARL training enables effective coordination by providing a systematic alternative to task-specific manual selection of the diversity target.
paragraphs.zh: 在合作式多智能体强化学习（MARL）中，智能体必须学会协调自身行动以实现共同目标。 有效协调的关键指标是行为多样性，即智能体在给定相同观测集时执行不同但互补的控制策略的潜力。 尽管行为多样性可以实现角色专业化并产生更丰富的联合行为，但其合适的水平高度依赖具体情境和任务，且调整起来通常成本高昂。 我们提出了自适应多样性控制（ADiCo），这是一种双时间尺度框架，能够在训练过程中在线调整行为多样性。 在快速时间尺度上，多样性控制（DiCo）将系统多样性调节至目标值。 在较慢的时间尺度上，极值搜索控制器（ESC）仅利用平均回合回报来调整该目标，无需显式模型或对多样性-性能景观的解析梯度。 我们在两个合作式MARL任务中六种配置下对ADiCo进行了评估，结果表明它能维持任务所需的多样性水平：当同质策略有益时保持低多样性，而当异质策略必要时则保持更高多样性。 通过这种自适应机制，ADiCo的平均性能与DiCo（通过网格搜索获得最佳多样性目标）和Unconstrained DiCo（允许多样性自然形成而不进行目标调节）相当或更优。 这些结果表明，将经典反馈控制融入MARL训练能够通过为任务特定的多样性目标手动选择提供系统性替代方案，从而实现有效协调。

paragraphs.en: In cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) [ 1 , 2 ] , a growing body of work has shown that behavioral diversity among agents can provide significant benefits, including the emergence of complementary roles, improved exploration, and greater resilience to disruptions [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 ] . Under the Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm, centralized information may be used during training while agents execute decentralized policies based on local observations. The resulting degree of behavioral diversity is shaped by architectural and learning-design choices such as parameter sharing, auxiliary objectives, and intrinsic rewards [ 8 ] . However, these approaches generally induce or encourage diversity without explicitly regulating its resulting magnitude to a desired, measurable level. Consider a team of delivery drones: if all packages are destined for the same neighborhood, similar behaviors may be sufficient, resulting in low diversity. In contrast, if packages must be delivered to different parts of a city, agents may need to specialize their routes, requiring greater behavioral diversity. The appropriate degree of diversity therefore depends on the task, motivating methods that can explicitly measure and regulate behavioral diversity according to task requirements.
paragraphs.zh: 在合作式多智能体强化学习（MARL）[ 1 , 2 ] 中，越来越多的研究表明，智能体之间的行为多样性可以带来显著益处，包括互补角色的出现、探索能力的提升以及对干扰的更强韧性 [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 ] 。 在集中式训练与去中心化执行（CTDE）范式下，训练过程中可以使用集中式信息，而智能体则根据局部观察执行去中心化的策略。 由此产生的行为多样性程度受架构和学习设计选择的影响，例如参数共享、辅助目标和内在奖励 [ 8 ] 。 然而，这些方法通常只是引入或鼓励多样性，却没有明确地将多样性的大小调节到期望的可衡量水平。 假设有一支配送无人机团队：如果所有包裹都送往同一社区，相似的行为可能已经足够，从而导致较低的多样性。 相反，如果包裹必须送达城市的不同区域，智能体可能需要对路线进行专门优化，从而需要更高的行为多样性。 因此，适当的多样性程度取决于具体任务，这也促使人们开发能够根据任务需求明确测量和调节行为多样性的方法。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we measure behavioral diversity using System Neural Diversity (SND) [ 9 ] , which aggregates pairwise differences between agents’ policies into a single system-level measure. To regulate this diversity, we use Diversity Control (DiCo) [ 4 ] , which represents each agent’s policy as the sum of a shared component and a dynamically scaled agent-specific component, allowing system diversity to be controlled toward a prescribed SND target. However, the appropriate diversity target is task-dependent and generally unknown a priori. We therefore formulate its selection as a feedback optimization problem and use Extremum Seeking Control (ESC) [ 10 ] , a model-free optimization technique used across domains including robotics, manufacturing and energy systems [ 11 , 12 ] . ESC applies small sinusoidal perturbations to the diversity target and processes the resulting variations in task performance to estimate the local direction of improvement, which is then used to adapt the nominal diversity setpoint.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们使用系统神经多样性（System Neural Diversity, SND）[9] 来衡量行为多样性，该方法将智能体策略之间的成对差异汇总为一个单一的系统级指标。 为了调节这种多样性，我们采用多样性控制（Diversity Control, DiCo）[4]，它将每个智能体的策略表示为共享组件与动态调整的智能体特定组件之和，从而可将系统多样性控制在预设的 SND 目标范围内。 然而，合适的多样性目标因任务而异，且通常无法事先确定。 因此，我们将该目标的选取问题构建为一个反馈优化问题，并使用极值寻优控制（Extremum Seeking Control, ESC）[10]——一种广泛应用于机器人、制造和能源系统等多个领域的无模型优化技术 [11, 12]。 ESC 通过对多样性目标施加微小的正弦扰动，并处理由此引起的任务性能变化，来估计局部改进方向，进而用于调整名义的多样性设定值。

paragraphs.en: We introduce ADiCo, a two-timescale framework that integrates ESC with DiCo to adapt behavioral diversity during cooperative MARL training using only scalar performance feedback, without requiring an explicit model or analytical gradient of the diversity–performance relationship.

paragraphs.en: We validate ADiCo on six configurations across two cooperative MARL tasks, demonstrating task-appropriate diversity adaptation and performance comparable to or better than grid-searched and unconstrained DiCo baselines without manual tuning of the diversity target.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在两个协作式 MARL 任务中，通过六种配置验证了 ADiCo，结果表明其能够根据任务需求进行多样性自适应，且性能与经过网格搜索和无约束的 DiCo 基线模型相当甚至更优，而无需手动调整多样性目标。

paragraphs.en: Behavioral diversity in cooperative MARL has been encouraged through a range of architectural and learning mechanisms. Selective parameter-sharing and agent-specific architectures allow policies to specialize to different degrees [ 16 , 18 , 19 , 20 ] , while methods based on latent variables, role representations, and intrinsic objectives explicitly encourage diverse behaviors or specialization [ 21 , 22 , 23 ] . These approaches primarily enable or promote heterogeneity, but generally do not expose the resulting magnitude of behavioral diversity as an explicit control variable. System Neural Diversity (SND) [ 9 ] addresses the measurement problem by quantifying policy-level heterogeneity through pairwise behavioral distances, while Diversity Control (DiCo) [ 4 ] uses this measure to regulate the system toward a prescribed diversity target, SND des \mathrm{SND}_{\mathrm{des}} . Although DiCo outlines an outer-loop procedure for adjusting desired diversity toward a user-specified performance level, it does not address the problem of locating an unknown reward-maximizing diversity target. This motivates adapting the desired diversity directly from task-performance feedback during training.

paragraphs.en: Adaptive hyperparameter optimization has also been studied within reinforcement learning. Population-Based Training (PBT) jointly adapts model parameters and hyperparameter schedules using a population of concurrently trained agents [ 26 ] , while Hyperparameter Optimization on the Fly (HOOF) adapts policy-gradient hyperparameters within a single training run by evaluating candidate policy updates using off-policy estimates [ 24 ] . Meta-gradient methods instead differentiate through the learning process to adapt differentiable hyperparameters online [ 25 ] . In our setting, the desired diversity is a control input to DiCo, and its effect on task performance is unknown and may change as policies learn. We therefore require a model-free controller that can adjust this target during training using scalar performance feedback, without access to an analytical gradient of the diversity-performance relationship.
paragraphs.zh: 自适应超参数优化在强化学习领域也得到了研究。 基于种群的训练（PBT）通过一个并行训练的智能体种群，同时调整模型参数和超参数调度方案 [ 26 ]；而在线超参数优化（HOOF）则通过在单次训练过程中使用离策略估计评估候选策略更新，来调整策略梯度方法的超参数 [ 24 ]。 相比之下，元梯度方法通过对学习过程进行微分，在线调整可微的超参数 [ 25 ]。 在我们的设定中，所需的多样性是 DiCo 的一个控制输入，其对任务性能的影响尚不明确，并可能随着策略的学习而发生变化。 因此，我们需要一个模型无关的控制器，能够在训练过程中利用标量性能反馈调整这一目标，而无需获取多样性与性能之间关系的解析梯度。

sents.en: In our setting, the desired diversity is a control input to DiCo, and its effect on task performance is unknown and may change as policies learn.
sents.zh: 在我们的设定中，所需的多样性是 DiCo 的一个控制输入，其对任务性能的影响尚不明确，并可能随着策略的学习而发生变化。

sents.en: We therefore require a model-free controller that can adjust this target during training using scalar performance feedback, without access to an analytical gradient of the diversity-performance relationship.
sents.zh: 因此，我们需要一个模型无关的控制器，能够在训练过程中利用标量性能反馈调整这一目标，而无需获取多样性与性能之间关系的解析梯度。

paragraphs.en: Extremum Seeking Control (ESC) meets these requirements by applying small periodic perturbations and using the resulting performance variations to estimate a local direction of improvement [ 10 , 11 ] . paragraphs.en: In this section, we present Adaptive Diversity Control (ADiCo), a framework for adapting behavioral diversity during cooperative MARL training.

sents.en: ESC addresses this problem by perturbing the target and processing the resulting changes in R k R_{k} to estimate a local direction of performance improvement.

paragraphs.en: This section evaluates ADiCo’s ability to adapt behavioral diversity across different task configurations and analyzes its convergence behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 本节评估了 ADiCo 在不同任务配置中适应行为多样性的能力，并分析了其收敛行为。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate ADiCo on two cooperative continuous-control tasks from the Vectorized Multi-Agent Simulator (VMAS) [ 31 ] : Navigation and Balance (Fig. 2 ). All experiments use three agents under partial observability, with episodes lasting at most 100 steps. We keep the team size fixed to simplify the analysis, although ADiCo is not limited to a fixed number of agents.

paragraphs.en: For each configuration, we compare ADiCo with two baselines. Grid-searched DiCo uses the best fixed SND target from { 0 , 0.3 , 0.5 , 0.8 , 1.0 , 1.3 , 1.5 , 1.8 , 2.0 } \{0,0.3,0.5,0.8,1.0,1.3,1.5,1.8,2.0\} , with a separate 12M-frame training run for each target. Unconstrained DiCo fixes the agent-specific scaling factor at one, allowing diversity to emerge without an explicit SND target. These baselines test whether online adaptation can match or improve upon both the best grid-searched target and freely emerging diversity. All methods use the same MARL algorithm, network architecture, and 12M-frame budget per training run.

paragraphs.en: In this section, we evaluate ADiCo across three key aspects: performance across task configurations, diversity adaptation from different initial targets, and training behavior under continuous ESC perturbations.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们从三个关键方面对 ADiCo 进行了评估：跨任务配置的性能、从不同初始目标出发的多样性适应能力，以及在持续 ESC 扰动下的训练行为。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate ADiCo across six configurations of two cooperative tasks. In Navigation, we vary the number of goals (1, 2, or 3) to change the need for specialization, using 3A- x x G to denote three agents with x x goals. In Balance, we vary ball Mass (2, 3, or 4) to change task difficulty while keeping the coordination structure the same, using 3A- x x M to denote three agents with ball Mass x x . In Navigation (Fig. 3 , top row), ADiCo adapts to high diversity (SND ≈ \approx 1.2–1.3) for 3A-3G, moderate diversity (SND ≈ \approx 0.8) for 3A-2G, and near-zero diversity for 3A-1G. It achieves reward comparable to grid-searched DiCo, with lower reward variance than Unconstrained DiCo. In Balance (bottom row), ADiCo maintains low diversity across all Mass configurations and matches the performance of DiCo with SND = 0. For Unconstrained DiCo, increasing diversity accompanies declining reward, with performance collapsing in the 3A-4M configuration. These results show that ADiCo automatically adapts toward low diversity when similar behaviors are beneficial and higher diversity when specialization helps. It achieves performance comparable to manually tuned DiCo without requiring configuration-specific grid search, while avoiding the excessive diversity observed with Unconstrained DiCo.

paragraphs.en: The previous experiments initialize ADiCo at SND = 0. To examine whether this choice affects the final diversity level, we test initial targets of 0, 0.5, and 1.0 on Navigation 3A-3G and compare them with DiCo using the same fixed targets. Fig. 4 (a) shows that ADiCo reaches a similar SND range ( ≈ \approx 1.2–1.3) from all three initial targets. Runs initialized at 0.5 and 1.0 reach this range faster than those initialized at 0. DiCo with SND = 0 or 0.5 achieves lower performance, while the best grid-searched target, SND = 1.0, produces longer episodes than ADiCo. These results show that ADiCo reaches similar diversity levels and performance across the tested initializations, while completing episodes faster than the fixed-target baselines. We next examine whether keeping ESC active remains beneficial after diversity settles.

paragraphs.en: ESC continues to perturb the diversity target even after it settles near a particular level. To examine whether continued adaptation remains useful, we compare ADiCo with a variant that monitors the gradient estimate and disables perturbations when a stopping criterion is met. This variant then holds the diversity target fixed for the remainder of training. Fig. 5 (a) shows that the frozen-target variant maintains SND near zero for 3A-1G, approximately 0.9 for 3A-2G, and approximately 1.0 for 3A-3G. These values are close to the best targets found through grid search. Once the target is frozen, the SND trajectories flatten as expected. In contrast, ADiCo with continued ESC adaptation achieves shorter episodes in 3A-3G and comparable episode lengths in the other configurations (Fig. 5 (b)). These results suggest that continued adaptation can remain beneficial after diversity appears to settle. However, this comparison does not separate the effect of perturbations from the benefit of further target updates, since the frozen-target variant disables both.

sents.en: Fig. 5 (a) shows that the frozen-target variant maintains SND near zero for 3A-1G, approximately 0.9 for 3A-2G, and approximately 1.0 for 3A-3G.

sents.en: In contrast, ADiCo with continued ESC adaptation achieves shorter episodes in 3A-3G and comparable episode lengths in the other configurations (Fig. 5 (b)).

sents.zh: 然而，这种比较并未区分扰动的影响与进一步更新目标所带来的好处，因为固定目标变体同时关闭了这两者。

paragraphs.en: While ADiCo uses mean episodic return to adapt diversity, changes in return are not always caused by diversity adjustments alone. Factors such as policy learning, environmental shifts, and adapting opponents also influence performance, complicating adaptation in adversarial or mixed-motive domains. Consequently, future work could explore alternative feedback signals and evaluation methods that better isolate the specific effect of diversity. Furthermore, because ADiCo relies on extremum seeking control, it risks converging to a local optimum of the performance signal rather than the globally optimal diversity target for the task. This limitation is compounded by the fact that ADiCo currently tunes only a single team-wide SND target, whereas distinct agents or roles may benefit from different diversity levels. Extending the framework with multidimensional ESC could allow multiple diversity targets to be adjusted from a shared performance signal, enabling more detailed control over team behavior. Finally, ADiCo adapts diversity exclusively during training rather than runtime execution. Because teams often need to alter behavior as conditions change within an episode, integrating ADiCo with event-based policy adaptation [ 32 ] could allow agents to dynamically adjust their diversity in response to runtime events.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然 ADiCo 使用平均回合回报来调整多样性，但回报的变化并不总是仅由多样性调整所引起。 策略学习、环境变化以及对抗对手的适应等因素也会影响性能，从而在对抗性或混合动机领域使适应性变得更加复杂。 因此，未来的研究可以探索替代的反馈信号和评估方法，以更好地分离多样性的特定影响。 此外，由于 ADiCo 依赖极值搜索控制，它可能会收敛到性能信号的局部最优，而非任务所需的全局最优多样性目标。 这一局限性还因 ADiCo 目前仅调整单个团队范围内的 SND 目标而加剧，而不同的智能体或角色可能受益于不同的多样性水平。 通过采用多维 ESC 扩展该框架，或许可以从共享的性能信号中调整多个多样性目标，从而实现对团队行为的更精细控制。 最后，ADiCo 仅在训练阶段调整多样性，而非在运行时执行过程中进行调整。 由于团队常常需要在回合内根据条件变化调整行为，将 ADiCo 与基于事件的政策适应方法 [32] 相结合，可能使智能体能够根据运行时的事件动态调整其多样性。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduced ADiCo, a framework that adapts team diversity during training using team-performance feedback. Across two cooperative tasks, ADiCo adjusts diversity to task-appropriate levels. Experiments with different initial setpoints further show that, in the tested configuration, users can begin with a rough diversity estimate and let ADiCo refine it without an explicit model of team dynamics. More broadly, ADiCo illustrates how model training can be viewed as a process whose adjustable components are optimized through feedback, much like machines in industrial systems. This perspective allows us to draw on established control techniques to improve the adaptability of learning systems.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们提出了 ADiCo——一个利用团队表现反馈在训练过程中调整团队多样性的框架。 在两项协作任务中，ADiCo 将多样性调整至适合任务的水平。 使用不同初始设定值进行的实验进一步表明，在测试的配置中，用户可以从一个粗略的多样性估计值开始，并让 ADiCo 对其进行优化，而无需明确的团队动态模型。 更广泛地说，ADiCo 展示了如何将模型训练视为一个通过反馈优化其可调组件的过程，这与工业系统中的机器非常相似。 这种视角使我们能够借鉴成熟的控制技术，以提升学习系统的适应性。
